title: Maharashtra may face warmer months as El Nino strengthens, IMD warns of summer heat - Mid-Day
full_text:
Representation pic
Maharashtra could face a warmer period ahead as El Nino strengthens over the Pacific, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) expecting the climate pattern to intensify further between October and December and potentially reach the âvery strong' category.
The developing El Nino is being closely watched for its possible impact on rainfall, temperatures and water resources. The IMD had forecast below-normal rainfall for the 2026 southwest monsoon, revising its forecast from 92 per cent to 90 per cent of the long-period average (LPA). The department said El Nino was weak in June and strengthened to moderate levels in July, with further strengthening possible towards the end of the year.
Senior IMD scientist SD Sanap, Pune, said: "The intensity of El Nino will start impacting from December. This year, due to the El Nino effect, extreme heat may be experienced during summer."
Sanap referred to the El Nino conditions of 2015 while explaining the possible implications of the current situation. According to him, Solapur has been among the districts worst affected by deficient rainfall, while parts of Pune, Nashik, Palghar and Raigad, particularly the ghat areas, have recorded comparatively higher rainfall.
The monsoon picture has varied sharply across Maharashtra. Some areas have received substantial rainfall, while others have experienced prolonged dry spells. That uneven distribution matters because a few days of heavy rain do not necessarily make up for rainfall deficits elsewhere. It can also affect soil moisture, groundwater recharge, reservoirs and rain-fed agriculture.
A weather system over the Bay of Bengal is currently increasing rainfall activity over parts of central and eastern India. The IMD has forecast very heavy rain in Vidarbha on September 24 and 25, followed by heavy rain on September 26. Thunderstorms and lightning are also expected. Marathwada has been warned of heavy rain on September 24, while parts of Madhya Maharashtra could see thunderstorms and strong surface winds through September 26. The spell could provide relief to rainfall-deficient areas, particularly in Vidarbha.
Rainfall-deficient districts could face greater pressure on water resources. Agriculture could be affected. The possible strengthening of El Nino adds another layer of uncertainty, with meteorologists watching temperatures, rainfall distribution, soil moisture and water availability as Maharashtra moves from the monsoon into winter.
>> Very heavy rain: Vidarbha, September 24-25
>> Heavy rain: Vidarbha, September 26
>> Heavy rain warning: Marathwada, September 24
>> Thunderstorms/strong winds: parts of Madhya Maharashtra through September 26
>> Longer-term watch: El Nino strengthening, water availability, summer temperatures
It does mean: a climate pattern that can influence Indian rainfall and temperatures. It does not mean: every part of Maharashtra will necessarily be dry or experience extreme heat. The IMD has stressed that the eventual impact will depend on El Nino as well as other oceanic and atmospheric conditions.
For Maharashtra, the key question will be not just how much rain falls, but where and when it falls
